subject: Staggered provisioning & MAP — Brightlane Dedicated capacity & eval plan
messages:
From: Alicia Tran <alicia.tran@brightlane.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Eval timeframe & provisioning questions for Dedicated / Private

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We kicked off an internal review and the two threads that matter for us right now are: (1) a short evaluation window to validate latency/cost for our inference workloads, and (2) a firm plan for capacity reservation if we proceed to Dedicated or Private.

Key asks from Brightlane:
- Example MAP we can sign up to that outlines evaluation milestones and procurement milestones (dates + owners).
- Lead times for Dedicated vs Private deployments (we need to understand order of magnitude for GPU procurement or cloud reservation).
- Suggested GPU pool sizing for a 12-month production ramp (starter / mid / scale scenarios).

We are targeting an internal decision by end of November. Can you send a one-page MAP and your recommended sizing scenarios? Also cc procurement@brightlane.com for any PO-level questions.

Appreciate it —
Alicia
Alicia Tran
Head of Platform Engineering | Brightlane Labs

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Tran <alicia.tran@brightlane.com>
Cc: procurement@brightlane.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Eval timeframe & provisioning questions for Dedicated / Private

Hi Alicia —

Attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a short checklist covering evaluation milestones and procurement handoffs. High-level notes:

- Evaluation: 2-week technical eval (sample workload provided by you) followed by a 2-week pilot (can run on our hosted infra or on a dedicated trial pool).
- Dedicated lead time (reserved pool): typically 6–10 weeks from PO + signed SOW (depends on cloud region and instance availability).
- Private (VPC / on-prem): 10–16 weeks on average (on-prem procurement + network/security review adds time).

I attached: Brightlane_MAP_v1.pdf (one-page MAP) and SOW_Brightlane_draft.docx.

Quick sizing guidance (starter / mid / scale) for the 12-month ramp you asked about:
- Starter: 4x H100-equivalent GPUs (focus: latency SLOs, lower throughput).
- Mid: 12x H100-equivalent GPUs (steady throughput, room for traffic spikes).
- Scale: 36+ GPUs (heavy throughput; shard across tranches to shorten delivery).

Notes on tranches: for both Dedicated and Private we recommend a staggered provisioning plan (3 tranches) to reduce upfront capex and allow us to validate model quantization and batching before each increase. For Brightlane's initial traffic profile, starting at the Starter -> Mid cadence minimizes cost risk.

Next steps: if this looks reasonable, can we set up a 30-minute alignment call next week with procurement and engineering to finalize the MAP timelines?

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Brightlane_MAP_v1.pdf (MAP, 1 page); SOW_Brightlane_draft.docx (SOW, draft)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Brightlane MAP — GPU sizing & lead-time plan (action items)

Ben / Karthik —

Looping you both in to confirm the sizing and lead-time guidance I sent to Brightlane. They want a MAP they can circulate internally and aim to decide end of November. Highlights / asks below:

Summary of what Alicia needs:
- MAP with concrete milestone dates and owners (evaluation -> pilot -> PO -> SOW sign -> capacity delivery).
- Clear lead-time ranges for Dedicated vs Private (they specifically asked for worst-case windows so procurement can plan).
- A recommended staggered provisioning plan to de-risk delivery.

My suggested dates for their MAP (assume we get PO & signed SOW by 2026-12-06):
- Week 0 (2026-11-30 to 2026-12-13): Technical eval + pilot (2w) — engineering leads: Brightlane + Redwood
- Week 2–4 (2026-12-14 to 2026-12-27): Procurement & SOW finalization — owners: procurement@brightlane.com, Redwood Sales Ops
- Week 4–12 (2026-12-28 to 2027-03-01): Tranche 1 delivery (starter pool) — dedicated: 6–10 weeks; private: 10–16 weeks
- Tranche 2 (2027-03-01 to 2027-05-01): Mid pool addition (4–8 weeks after tranche 1, depending on availability)
- Tranche 3 (2027-06-01+): Scale pool (timing depends on rate of traffic and budget)

Sizing assumptions used (please sanity-check):
- "H100-equivalent" metric assumes typical Gen2 model mix (large chat + fine-tuned retrieval).
- Starter (4 GPUs) targets P50 latency under 150ms for 2k concurrent requests/day.
- Mid (12 GPUs) targets 10k concurrent requests/day with autoscaling headroom.
- Scale (36+) for 50k+ concurrent/day or heavy batch workloads.

Action items:
- Ben: please confirm that the 6–10 week committed delivery window is feasible for a Dedicated pool when we sequence in tranches (I want to be conservative on the MAP). If we can tighten the lower bound to 5 weeks in certain regions that helps their procurement.
- Karthik: confirm Private/on-prem packaging lead times (network/security sign-off assumptions) and any standard prechecks we should require in the MAP (e.g., on-prem rack power / rack mount silent checklist).

Let me know by EOD Monday so I can update the MAP and send to Brightlane.

Thanks —
Sofia
